hook.line: Sooner or later someone says "you said it was urgent!" and you need to answer "I never said that". In Spanish that little *no* changes the verb that follows, and getting it right makes you sound precise instead of defensive.
hook.en: I didn't say it was urgent.

examples.es: No es que no quiera, es que no puedo.
examples.en: It's not that I don't want to, it's that I can't.
He didn't say it was urgent.
I saw that Vale was angry.

examples.es: No vi que Vale estuviera enojada.
examples.en: I didn't see that Vale was angry.

examples.es: No oí que sonara el teléfono.
examples.en: I didn't hear the phone ring.

rule:
After *vi que*, *oí que* or *dijo que*, you use the ordinary past verb: *Vi que Vale estaba enojada.* *Dijo que era urgente.* You are vouching for it.

Put *no* in front and you now have a choice, and it says who is vouching.

Keep the ordinary verb and you still vouch for it: it was true, and someone missed it or left it out. *No vi que estabas ahí.* You were there, and I missed you. *No dijo que era urgente.* It was urgent, and he left that out.

Switch to the *-ra* form, as after *no creo que*, and nobody vouches: *estaba* becomes *estuviera*, *era* becomes *fuera*, *tenía* becomes *tuviera*, *llegó* becomes *llegara*, *sonó* becomes *sonara*. *No dije que fuera urgente.* I never claimed that. *No vi que estuviera enojada.* I saw no sign of it.

Three cases leave no choice. With *nadie* or *nada*, use the *-ra* form: *No vi que llegara nadie.* After *no veo que*, use the wish form: *No veo que esté enojada.* *No es que* denies the idea, so it takes the wish form too: *No es que no quiera, es que no puedo.*

If you missed something that did happen, you can also use the infinitive, as in *la vi salir*: *No oí sonar el teléfono.*

English keeps one verb for both. Spanish tells you who stands behind the claim.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the subjunctive after negated verbs of perception and speech. The *no* lets you stop backing the claim; if you still back it, the indicative stays.

yourTurn.prompt: I didn't say it was urgent. Choose *fuera* or *era*: No dije que ___ urgente.
yourTurn.why: After *no dije que* the verb takes the *-ra* form: *fuera*.

yourTurn.prompt: I saw that Vale was angry. Choose *estaba* or *estuviera*: Vi que Vale ___ enojada.
yourTurn.why: With no *no*, you are vouching for it, so the ordinary past is *estaba*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I didn't see that Vale was angry.
yourTurn.answer: No vi que Vale estuviera enojada.
accept: No vi que Vale estuviera enojada
No vi que Vale estaba enojada.
No vi que Vale estaba enojada
yourTurn.why: Both work. *Estuviera* says you saw no sign of it, and *estaba* says she was angry and you missed it.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I didn't hear the phone ring.
yourTurn.answer: No oí que sonara el teléfono.
accept: No oí que sonara el teléfono
No oí que el teléfono sonara.
No oí que sonó el teléfono.
yourTurn.why: *Sonara* doesn't vouch for the ring. If it rang and you missed it, *No oí que sonó* and *No oí sonar el teléfono* work too.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: He didn't say it was urgent.
yourTurn.why: Both work. *Fuera* doesn't vouch for it, and *era* says it was urgent and he left that out.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: Dijo que Vale tenía la culpa.
yourTurn.answer: No dijo que Vale tuviera la culpa.
accept: No dijo que Vale tuviera la culpa

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: Vi que llegaba Hernando.
Say: It's not that I don't want to, it's that I can't.
yourTurn.answer: No es que no quiera, es que no puedo.
accept: No es que no quiera, es que no puedo
yourTurn.why: The denied half takes *quiera*; the true half stays ordinary: *puedo*.

pitfalls.wrong: No veo que Vale está enojada.
pitfalls.right: No veo que Vale esté enojada.
pitfalls.why: Almost. You can't vouch for what you say you don't see, so *no veo que* takes the wish form: *esté*.

pitfalls.wrong: No es que no quiero, es que no puedo.
pitfalls.right: No es que no quiera, es que no puedo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *No es que* denies the idea, so the verb takes the wish form: *quiera*.
Almost. A denied sighting takes the *-ra* form: *llegara*.
Almost. Without *no* you are reporting what you saw, so use the ordinary past.

personal: Think of something people assume about you that isn't true. Deny it: *No dije que…*, or *No es que…*
